drhp.business: Beekay Steel manufactures a portfolio of long steel products — hot-rolled sections, bright bars, structural steel, special profiles and Turbo TMT bars — serving the construction, infrastructure, automotive, engineering and railways sectors. It operates a non-proprietary manufacturing business comprising job work for an institutional steel partner, alongside a proprietary business spanning TMT bars and automotive/engineering steel.
drhp.expansion: Beekay Steel's Southern Odisha (Cuttack) investment programme reached a key milestone in FY 2025-26, with Phase 1 substantially completed and commercialised, transitioning the project from an investment phase to an operating asset with capital work-in-progress progressively capitalised into operating assets. The Company has commenced mobilisation for Phase 2 of the Southern Odisha expansion, planned to be funded through internal accruals and Rs. 500 Cr of long-term debt over the next five years, to provide a further platform for scale.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- India's steel demand is expected to grow at ~7-9% annually in FY 2025-26, broadly in line with economic growth.
- Infrastructure spending under Bharatmala, Sagarmala, Dedicated Freight Corridors and metro expansions is sustaining demand for long and structural steel.
- Rising urbanisation and real estate growth, with India's urban population projected to reach ~600 Mn by 2030, is accelerating demand for steel-intensive construction.
- Affordable housing demand under PMAY, estimated at ~45 Mn units by 2030, is expected to sustain demand for construction-grade long products.
- Consolidated revenue grew …

The Company has commenced mobilisation for Phase 2 of the Southern Odisha expansion, planned to be funded through internal accruals and Rs. 500 Cr of long-term debt over the next five years, to provide a further platform for scale.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Insufficient availability of funds for capital expenditure may impact the Company's ability to pursue growth initiatives and sustain cost competitiveness.
- Fluctuations in foreign exchange rates may adversely affect the profitability of export operations.
- Intensifying competition, including the entry of new players, may impact the Company's market share and pricing power.
- The ability to attract and retain skilled talent remains a key challenge for the steel industry, given rising attrition levels and operational complexities.
- A decline in product quality can negatively affect the Company's brand and revenue.
- Poor R&D and the threat of technological obsolescence affect a large part of the steel market (SWOT: Threats).
- Substitution of steel by alternative materials such as aluminium and plastics poses a structural threat to demand (SWOT: Threats).
- Recession in other countries can result in dumping of material into the domestic market, pressuring pricing (SWOT: Threats).

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Trebling revenues over the next four years beginning FY 2026-27 through a structurally stronger, deeper-talent, more disciplined organisation.

themes.title: Railway rolling-stock & component capex
themes.need: A ~INR2.65 lakh cr Railways capital outlay and a pending ~1-lakh-wagon tender ('anytime this year' per JWL) drive rolling-stock, wheelsets, springs, castings, bogie components and interiors - with deep import-substitution (Neetu Yoshi 544434 castings; Airfloa 544516 interiors; Concord 543619 electronics). TITAGARH/TEXRAIL/JWL lead wagons; RVNL/IRCON/GPTINFRA on rail EPC.
themes.driver: Indian Railways large wagon tender award (next 1-2 quarters); wheelset plant ramp; Vande Bharat / Kavach orders.

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.
